sentences.text: JUDGMENT

The plaintiff has filed this suit under Order VII Rule 1 of C.P.C., seeking for an order of permanent injunction restraining the defendant, her agents and servants from interfering with her possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and also grant such other reliefs.

2. The plaint averments in brief :
It is the case of the plaintiff that her father had entered into a sale agreement with respect to land bearing survey O.S.No.3848/2017 No.26 and survey Nos.4/1 & 4/2 situated at Geddalahalli Village, K.R.Puram, Bengaluru with its previous owner Smt.Theresamma and I.F.Dominic, wife and children of late Ignisiappa on 2.09.1989 for a sale consideration of Rs.6,90,000/-, but they failed to execute the Sale Deed in his name.
Hence her father had filed a suit against them in O.S.No.4955/1991 before CCH No.16, Bengaluru, wherein they entered into compromise on 18.03.1994.
Accordingly a Compromise Decree was drawn on 26.03.1994.

As per the compromise decree the plaintiff was allotted 14 sites in Survey No.26 i.e., site Nos.1, 2, 13, 14, 28,
29, 41, 42, 56, 57, 49, 68, 71 and 72. Out of which Site Nos.57 and 58 are corner sites.

Also he got 10 sites in Survey Nos.4/1 and 4/2 bearing Nos.10, 11, 20, 27, 28, 32, 33,
34, 43 and 44, each measuring 30 X 40 feet.
The revenue records were transferred to her father's name and he was regularly paying taxes to the BBMP and he has been in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property since 1989.
The plaintiff's father out of love and affection gifted her Site No.42 i.e., suit schedule property under Gift Deed dated:11.05.2017 registered in Document No.BNS-1-01774-2017-18 in C.D.No.BNS0592.
She has applied for transfer of katha to her name.

In the month of March 2017 the defendant started to interfere with her possession on the ground that she has purchased Site O.S.No.3848/2017 No.22, Katha No.62, Assessment No.75 of Geddalahalli Village, K.R.Puram, Bengaluru bounded on East by :
Property No.17, West by : Road, North by : Property No.21, South by : Property No.23, measuring East to West: 40 feet and North to South: 30 feet having purchased the same from I.F.Dominic under a registered Sale Deed dated:28.08.1979.
On verification of the same with her father, the plaintiff came to know that the defendant is no way connected with the suit schedule property.

Even though the plaintiff and her father tried to convince her regarding the identity and confusion of the site purchased by her, she refused to do so and lodged a complaint against her father before Hennur Police Station, Bengaluru.
The police on verifying of the documents asked the defendant to approach the civil court as the dispute is civil in nature.

But Thara Sophia N vs Padma Jain on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188457786/
2 again on 5.06.2017 the defendant tried to interfere with the plaintiff's possession.

sentences.text: Hence this suit.
3. The defendant in her written statement has specifically denied the plaint averments.

It is her contention that she is the absolute owner of the property bearing site No.22, Katha No.62,
Assessment No.75 of Geddalahalli Village, K.R.Puram Hobli, Bengaluru, bounded on the East by :
Property bearing Site No.17, West by :
O.S.No.3848/2017 Road, North by : Site No.21 and South by : Site No.23, hereinafter referred to as Site No.22 having purchased the same under a registered Sale Deed dated:7.10.1997 from one I.F.Dominic.
Her vendor had purchased the land in survey No.26 from one Thayappa under a registered Sale Deed dated:4.10.1965.
The defendant has been regularly paying the property tax with respect to Site No.22.
Since 1997 she has been in possession of Site No.22.
On 5.06.2003 the BDA had issued notice to the defendant stating that her site is subject matter of acquisition.

The BDA had issued award notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act vide Document No.LAC No.G36/2003- 04, dated:12.10.2004 awarding a compensation with respect of the acquired site promising to award compensation.
As such she did not construct building in Site No.22.
On 30.11.2016 BDA on conducting survey submitted its report stating that the defendant's site falls within Railway Buffer Zone.
Thereafter the defendant and other land owners have approached the Railway Authorities for joint survey.
Also survey measurement was done by BBMP.
The Junior Engineer, BBMP, Horamavu has sent a survey sketch along with a letter dated:28.08.2017 to the South Western Railways.
She has also applied for joint survey and NOC from Railways.
The Railway Authorities have conducted the survey and she is O.S.No.3848/2017 currently awaiting NOC from South Western Railways.
The plaintiff's father is interfering in her possession of her site bearing No.22.
When she lodged a complaint before Hennur Police Station in January 2017, they issued NCR dated:23.07.2017.
The plaintiff has not approached the court with clean hands.
Further Site No.42, which is already been transferred to one Mr.Basith Mahboob Shariff.
Hence, prayed that the suit be dismissed.
4. The plaintiff got examined herself as P.W.1 and marked the documents Exs.P.1 to 11.

The defendant got examined herself as D.W.1 and marked the documents Exs.D.1 to 45.
5.
Heard the arguments.
Both sides have filed written arguments.

6. My learned Predecessor has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the plaintiff proves that she is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as on the date of filing of the suit ?
2. Whether the plaintiff further proves the alleged interference by the defendant ?

7. My findings to the above issues are as under:
 ISSUE No.1 - Negative,
 ISSUE No.2 - Negative,
 ISSUE No.3 - Negative,
 ISSUE No.4 - As per the final order,
for the following :
 REASONS 8. ISSUE Nos.1 to 3 : In the present suit the plaintiff has sought to declare that she is in lawful possession of the suit schedule property and defendant is interfering in her possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.
As these issues are inter-related, they are taken up together for discussion.

9. It is the specific case of the plaintiff that her father had gifted her the plaint schedule property bearing site no 42 under a registered gift deed dated 11.5.2017.Her father by name Nathan had entered into an agreement of sale dated 2.9.1989 for a sale consideration of Rs O.S.No.3848/2017 6,90,000/- with one Smt.Theresamma and I.F.Dominic wife and children of late Ignisiappa who had purchased the property from the original vendor vide Sale Deed dated 5.3.1969.
As they failed to execute a Sale Deed, her father filed O.S No.4955/1991 in the Court of the Additional City Civil Judge (CCH-16), Bengaluru, there they entered into a compromise on 18.3.1994.
Accordingly a decree was drawn on 26.3.1994 by the said Court.

It is further stated that in terms of the Compromise Decree, the Plaintiff's father was allotted 14 sites in Survey No.26, bearing Nos. 1, 2, 13,
14, 28, 29, 41, 42, 56, 57, 49, 68, 71, 72 out of which Site No. 57 and 58 are Corner sites.
Similarly, he has also got 10 sites in Survey No.4/1 and 4/2 which are bearing Nos.10, 11, 20, 27, 28, 32, 33, 34, 43 and 44 each site measuring 30 ft. X 40 ft.
Copy of the Compromise decree and the layout plan is said to be produced with said decree.
All the revenue documents stands in the name of the father of the plaintiff.
Further in March 2017 defendant is alleged to have interfered in her possession on the ground that she has purchased Site No.22 from I.F.Dominic under a registered Sale Deed dated 28.8.1979.
On verification they came to know that site purchased by the defendant is in no way connected with suit schedule property.

But defendant lodged complaint in Hennur Police station,
the police on verification of the documents O.S.No.3848/2017 advised the defendant to approach civil court as dispute is civil in nature.
In view of the defendant's interference with plaintiff's possession of the suit schedule property she has filed this suit.

10. On other hand, defendant has contended that her vendor, I.F.Dominic had purchased the land bearing Survey No.26 situated at Geddalahalli Village, K.R. Puram, Bengaluru South Taluk, from one Thayappa, S/.o.Byanna vide registered Sale Deed dated 04.10.1965, registered in the Office of the Sub- Registrar, Bengaluru South Taluk.

The said I.F.Dominic had made a Layout Plan in respect of the sites situated in Survey No.26 and thereafter in respect of the said Layout Plan, he had sold Thara Sophia N vs Padma Jain on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188457786/
4 the Site bearing No.22 in her favour.

sentences.text: She has also obtained a Katha in respect of the said property.
The defendant has also been paying the Property Taxes regularly in respect of the said property.
B-Khata stands in her name.
Also encumbrance and electricity bills stands in her name.
She has further alleged that with respect to Site No.22 the Plaintiff's father has intentionally mis-identified it as Site No.42 by creating his own layout plan.
The topographical location, boundaries and measurements of the Site belonging to the defendant has no resemblance whatsoever to the Site claimed by the Plaintiff.

Once it came to the knowledge of the Plaintiff that electricity O.S.No.3848/2017 connection was obtained by the defendant in respect to Site No.22, the Plaintiff's father has intentionally created fake layout plan and has executed a Gift Deed dated 11.03.2017 in favor of his daughter in respect a Site Number that is mentioned in the so called Compromise Decree dated:26.03.1994.
This was done by the Plaintiff only with an intention to extort monetary settlement from the defendant.
Also she has stated about proceedings before B.D.A., acquisition and she has sought permission from South Western Railway to put up construction of the building in the said site.
Hence prayed to dismiss the suit.
11. The advocate of plaintiff in support of his contention has relied upon the decision reported in (2008)4SCC 594;(2019)SCC 692.

On other hand, advocate for defendant has relied upon the decisions reported in (2006) 5 SCC 466, 2024SCC online SC 169,W.P No 19003/2022 dated 2/8/2023, ILR 2005 KAR 884, ILR 2002 KAR 2699.
12.
The Plaintiff in support of her case got herself examined as P.W.1.
In her affidavit filed in lieu of her examination in chief she has reiterated the facts stated in the plaint.

Further she has got marked 11 documents namely Gift Deed dated 11/5/2017 -ExP1, BBMP property register extract- Ex.P.2,
BBMP property tax paid receipt- O.S.No.3848/2017 Ex.P.3 and Ex.P3(a), Certified copy of the order sheet in O.S.No.
4955/1991-Ex.P.4, Certified copy of the Plaint in O.S.No. 4955/1991- Ex.P.5, Certified copy of the Compromise Petition in O.S.No.4955/1991-Ex.P.6, Certified copy of the Decree copy in O.S.No.4955/1991-Ex.P.7, 2 photographs- Ex.P.8 and 9, C.D.-Ex.P.10 and Layout plan of Survey No.26 signed by the President of Gedalahalli Gram Panchayat on 6.01.2007-Ex.P.11.
13.
Further the defendant in support of her contention has got herself examined as D.W.1.
In her affidavit filed in lieu of her examination in chief she has reiterated the facts stated in the written statement.

She has furnished the following documents namely:Layout Plan-Ex.D.1, Certified copy of No Encumbrance Certificate of Site No.22 in Survey No.26-Ex.D.2, Certified copy of No Encumbrance Certificate of Site Nos.42 and 43 in Survey No.26-Ex.D.3, Certified copy of Judgment in O.S.No.2460/2010 is marked at Ex.D.4.

sentences.text: In the cross examination of PW1 she admitted that sale agreement which was entered was not a registered document and it is with her father.
She has denied the suggestion that Site No.22 mentioned in the written statement is part of the compromise decree-ExP6.
It is elicited that the previous owner had issued an irrevocable GPA in her father's name.

It is elicited that her father did O.S.No.3848/2017 not get a registered Sale Deed executed with respect to 14 sites on the basis of compromise decree, but he executed a Gift Deed in her favor in the year 2017.
15.

In view of the aforesaid oral and documentary evidence placed by the plaintiff, it is at first necessary to refer to condition No.5 of the compromise petition filed in O.S.No. 4955/1991-ExP6 which reads as under:
"5. All the other expenses for processing various documents for Registration of the above said site shall be borne by the Plaintiff.
The Defendants have executed an irrevocable General Power of Attorney in favor of the Plaintiff, with full liberty to deal with the foregoing sites in the manner of his choice."

16. On plain reading of the afore-mentioned condition No.5 of Compromise Petition, one can safely say that defendants therein had executed irrevocable General Power of Attorney to the plaintiff's father for the purpose of registration of the site at his expense, also to proceed with the sites as per his choice.
As such it can safely said that the father of the plaintiff herein had to first get a registered sale as per compromise petition.

Also from the cross examination of P.W.1 it can be safely said that her O.S.No.3848/2017 father did not a get registered Sale Deed in his name after the Compromise Decree.
17.

In view of the discussion made supra, it can be safely said that father of the plaintiff was not the owner of the property but only a GPA holder, merely because he had a irrevocable GPA does not make him the owner of the property.
Further on perusal of the registered Gift Deed-Ex.P.1 it is observed that Nathan is shown as the DONOR, in page 2 of the said Gift Deed it says that "DONOR herein is the sole and absolute owner".
Also no registered deed is forth coming to show that the Site No.42 was registered under a Sale Deed in the name of Sri.Nathan, the father of the plaintiff.
As such the decree has not been acted upon and title and ownership of the properties covered under the compromise petition does not stand in the name of the father of the plaintiff.

Hence it can be safely said that he not being the owner of the property has no right to gift the property as its owner as mentioned in the Gift Deed, as he has no valid title to execute the Gift Deed-ExP1.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that the plaintiff claims possession of the suit schedule property i.e., site bearing No.22.

To prove her possession she has furnished Gift Deed-Ex.P.1, BBMP property register extract- Ex.P.2, BBMP O.S.No.3848/2017 property tax paid receipt- Ex.P3 and Ex.P.3(a), two photographs-Exs.P.8 and 9, C.D.-Ex.P.10, Layout plan of Survey No.26 signed by the President of Gedalahalli Gram Panchayat on 6.01.2007-ExP11.
With respect to Gift Deed this court has already made an observation regarding title, it is not of much help to the plaintiff to prove the possession.

19. In the cross examination of PW1 she has stated that she could not get the katha transferred to her name as defendant interfered with it and defendant had given a letter to BBMP and she has a copy of the said letter, but plaintiff has not furnished any document from BBMP stating that they are not issuing khatha in her name due to the objection on the part of the defendant.

Also she has not furnished the copy of the letter said to have been given by defendant to BBMP .
20.
It is elicited in the cross examination of P.W.1 that they have constructed shed in the site without permission.
Also they have obtained electricity and water connection to the site.

Even though she stated that she would furnish BESCOM payment receipts and copy of the layout plan of 14 sites as per Ex.P.6, but till date plaintiff has made no efforts to furnish the aforesaid documents.

Also as per her evidence she has not been able to get encumbrance O.S.No.3848/2017 certificate due to the objection of the defendant but she has not furnished any document in support of her contention.
21. It becomes necessary to refer to the further cross examination of PW1 wherein she has admitted that Ex.P.11-Layout plan pertains to Survey No.26 Lourdes Nagar Layout plan.
It is elicited that said layout was named by her father Nathan and Dominic.
The pleadings of the plaintiff and affidavit filed in lieu of her examination in chief are silent regarding of formation of Lourdesnagar Layout.
In the Gift Deed-Ex.P.1it is stated that Site No.42 is situated in Inasiappa Layout.
As such there is contradictions regarding the location of Site No. 42 i.e., suit schedule property.

22. Here itself it is necessary to refer to the cross examination of D.W.1 wherein nothing has been elicited to prove the alleged interference in plaintiff's possession in March 2017 or due to her objection plaintiff is not able to get revenue records transferred to her.

But from the oral and documentary evidence of D.W.1 it can be safely said that she is in possession of Site No.22 and has approached the South Western Railways seeking permission to put up construction in Site No.22 as per rules and regulations.
Also as per Ex.D.33 South Western Railways have issued O.S.No.3848/2017 NOC, dated:5.03.2018 permitting the defendant herein to put up construction in Site No.22.
She has been regularly paying property tax to Site No.22 and BESCOM bills, also she has got no encumbrance certificate.

23. In view of the aforesaid oral and documentary evidence placed before the court and also taking into consideration the decisions relied by both sides, it is pertinent to note that plaintiff has to prove that she is in lawful possession of suit schedule property.
As such the burden of proving the said issue solely lies upon the plaintiff.

As discussed supra, the plaintiff has failed to prove the ownership over the suit schedule property as her father did not title to execute a Gift Deed in her favour with respect to the suit schedule property.
The layout plan-Ex.P.11 is with respect to Lourdes Nagar Layout wherein Site No.42 is situated.

Her pleadings are silent regarding the formation of Lourdes Thara Sophia N vs Padma Jain on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188457786/
7 Nagar Layout.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But in the Gift Deed-Ex.P.1 it is stated that Site No.42 is situated in Inasiappa Layout.
The reason as to why the layout name has been changed with respect to suit schedule property is not explained by the plaintiff.

As such there is contradictions regarding the location of Site No.42 i.e.,
suit schedule property.
Hence it can be safely said the plaintiff has not proved the exact location of the suit schedule property.
It is pertinent to note that the plaintiff has chosen not to furnish the original layout plan said to have been produced in O.S.No.4955/1991.
Also the Khatha and encumbrance with respect suit schedule property does not stand in the name of the plaintiff.
Even though it is contended that due to defendant's objection the concerned authorities have not transferred the same to her.
But when the plaintiff has approached the court for declaration on the ground of alleged interference, it is for the plaintiff to furnish evidence to prove the same.
Admittedly she has obtained BESCOM connection to the suit schedule property wherein a shed is built, but she has not furnished the BESCOM bills.
The tax paid receipt to BBMP is in the name of J.L.Nathan.

The non furnishing of the said documents clearly goes to show that plaintiff has not placed any convincing material before the court to prove that she is in lawful possession of the suit schedule property.

When the plaintiff has failed to prove her lawful possession over the suit schedule property in view of the discussion made supra, it is held that plaintiff has failed to prove that the defendant has interfered in her possession of the suit schedule property.
Hence this court is of the considered view that the plaintiff has not made out a ground for the grant of the reliefs prayed by her.
In O.S.No.3848/2017 view of the discussion made supra, I proceed to answer the Issue Nos.1 to 3 in the Negative.
25. ISSUE No.4:

In view of my findings on Issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiff is hereby dismissed with cost.
Draw decree accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The plaintiff has filed this suit under Order VII Rule 1 of C.P.C., seeking for an order of permanent injunction restraining the defendant, her agents and servants from interfering with her possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and also grant such other reliefs.
Hence her father had filed a suit against them in O.S.No.4955/1991 before CCH No.16, Bengaluru, wherein they entered into compromise on 18.03.1994.
On verification of the same with her father, the plaintiff came to know that the defendant is no way connected with the suit schedule property.
Even though the plaintiff and her father tried to convince her regarding the identity and confusion of the site purchased by her, she refused to do so and lodged a complaint against her father before Hennur Police Station, Bengaluru.
The police on verifying of the documents asked the defendant to approach the civil court as the dispute is civil in nature.
Her vendor had purchased the land in survey No.26 from one Thayappa under a registered Sale Deed dated:4.10.1965.
Since 1997 she has been in possession of Site No.22.
On 5.06.2003 the BDA had issued notice to the defendant stating that her site is subject matter of acquisition.
The BDA had issued award notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act vide Document No.LAC No.G36/2003- 04, dated:12.10.2004 awarding a compensation with respect of the acquired site promising to award compensation.
On 30.11.2016 BDA on conducting survey submitted its report stating that the defendant's site falls within Railway Buffer Zone.
opennyai_summary.issue:
6. My learned Predecessor has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the plaintiff proves that she is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as on the date of filing of the suit ?
2. Whether the plaintiff further proves the alleged interference by the defendant ?
O.S.No.3848/2017 Thara Sophia N vs Padma Jain on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188457786/
3 3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief of permanent injunction as sought for ?
4. What Order or Decree ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On verification they came to know that site purchased by the defendant is in no way connected with suit schedule property.
In view of the defendant's interference with plaintiff's possession of the suit schedule property she has filed this suit.
Once it came to the knowledge of the Plaintiff that electricity O.S.No.3848/2017 connection was obtained by the defendant in respect to Site No.22, the Plaintiff's father has intentionally created fake layout plan and has executed a Gift Deed dated 11.03.2017 in favor of his daughter in respect a Site Number that is mentioned in the so called Compromise Decree dated:26.03.1994.
This was done by the Plaintiff only with an intention to extort monetary settlement from the defendant.
Hence it can be safely said that he not being the owner of the property has no right to gift the property as its owner as mentioned in the Gift Deed, as he has no valid title to execute the Gift Deed-ExP1.
As discussed supra, the plaintiff has failed to prove the ownership over the suit schedule property as her father did not title to execute a Gift Deed in her favour with respect to the suit schedule property.
Hence it can be safely said the plaintiff has not proved the exact location of the suit schedule property.
But when the plaintiff has approached the court for declaration on the ground of alleged interference, it is for the plaintiff to furnish evidence to prove the same.
Admittedly she has obtained BESCOM connection to the suit schedule property wherein a shed is built, but she has not furnished the BESCOM bills.
The tax paid receipt to BBMP is in the name of J.L.Nathan.
The non furnishing of the said documents clearly goes to show that plaintiff has not placed any convincing material before the court to prove that she is in lawful possession of the suit schedule property.
When the plaintiff has failed to prove her lawful possession over the suit schedule property in view of the discussion made supra, it is held that plaintiff has failed to prove that the defendant has interfered in her possession of the suit schedule property.
Hence this court is of the considered view that the plaintiff has not made out a ground for the grant of the reliefs prayed by her.
